Hello to all from r/liverpool, this is v/liverpool!
Yeah, I avoid reddit as much as I can, would be nice to see everyone move here as Liverpool has always seem pro free speech to me.

I want to make my intentions for this subverse very clear, so everyone knows what to expect from the start.

The current rules:

1) Keep discussion related to the topic of this subverse (obvious)

2) Try to be nice to each other. I understand once in a while, you may get angry. That is fine. However, if you are only here to be nasty and never contribute any discussion, you will be banned. This may sound subjective, and I hate subjective rules. However, I'm not sure how to word this more clearly. As long most of your posts are on-topic, you are fine. Also, I will give you a warning before you are banned. You won't wake up one day and find that you were mysteriously banned.

As far as moderation:

The only reasons I will delete a post is if it is off-topic or does not further any discussion. I will never delete a post because I don't agree with it. If I ban a user or delete a post, I will let the community know. If the majority of users disagree with my ban, I will reverse it.

Concerning the future:

As of now, the two rules listed above should be enough. However, if in the future I decide the subverse could use a new rule, I will bring it up with the community. If the community agrees with the rule, I will implement it. If the community does not agree, I won't implement the rule. I think this covers everything I want to mention about the running of this subverse. Over all, I want this to be a fun place, and I want to keep moderation to a minimum. I believe minimal intervention is the best way to run a community like this.

Concerning CSS

I'm not well-versed in CSS, and I really don't feel like putting in the time to learn how to properly code it. As such, this subverse will look like this until/unless someone who is well-versed in CSS comes around to design something custom. The most I will do is create link flairs if I feel more are needed.

As @heratiki mentioned it’s already a feature, but only shown when users hit the limit. Why this is good: it doesn’t influence user behaviour until necessary. If they never hit the limit through their natural behaviour, then it practically and literally doesn’t affect them. If they do hit the limit, they are given the explanation.

One interesting thing about user behaviour: don’t give them ideas. Your explanation is well-written, but it introduces the ideas of vote brigading and spam, which may not even be on the user’s mind. When dealing with a large, unknown quantity like the internet, it’s best not to give them any ideas. Say “use your votes wisely” instead of “don’t vote brigade”.
